passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis should be read together with our audited consolidated financial statements and notes appearing in Item 18 below. General Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates Our significant accounting policies are described in Item 18. Financial Statements – Note 2. Our results of operations and financial condition are based on our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP). The preparation of the consolidated financial statements requires management to select accounting policies, and to make estimates, assumptions and judgments that involve the accounting policies described below that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements. Significant changes in assumptions and/or conditions and changes in our critical accounting policies could materially impact our operating results and financial condition. We believe our most critical accounting policies relate to: • Revenue Recognition; • Impairment of Long-Lived Assets and Goodwill; • Income Taxes; • Post-employment Benefits Liabilities. Revenue Recognition We generate revenues primarily from fixed-price long-term contracts involving the design, development, manufacture and integration of defense systems and products. In addition, to a lesser extent, we provide non-defense systems and products as well as support and services for our systems and products. Revenues from our contracts are principally recognized using the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 606. We assess contractual arrangements at inception according to the five-step model of ASC 606. We recognize revenues for each of the identified performance obligations when our customer obtains control of the products or services. The assessment of when the customer obtains control involves significant judgments, including, inter alia, whether there is an alternative use for a product, the contract terms, assessment of the enforceable rights for payments, and technical or contractual constraints. As a practical expedient we may occasionally account for group of performance obligations or contracts collectively, as opposed to individually by using the “portfolio approach” or the “series of distinct goods and services” method. Under the “portfolio approach” method, the Company may combine individual performance obligations, if the goods or services of the individual performance obligations have similar characteristics and the Company reasonably expects that the effect on the financial statements of applying this guidance would not defer materially from applying the guidance to the individual contracts or performance obligations within that portfolio. In addition, as a practical expedient, the Company does not assess the existence of a significant financing component when the difference between payment and transfer of control is less than one year. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: We attempt to identify, manage and mitigate risks to our business. However, some of these risks are not within our control, and risks and uncertainty cannot be fully eliminated or predicted. Prior to investing in our ordinary shares, you should carefully consider the following risk factors as well as other information contained in this annual report. The risk factors presented below may not necessarily be in order of importance or probability of occurrence. Risks Related to Our Operations A cyber or security attack or other similar incident resulting in a breach, disruption or failure in our or our supply chain's digital environment, or of our products, could adversely affect us. Our operations depend heavily on the continued and secure functioning of our varied digital environment software and hardware that stores, processes and transmits data within the Company and from and to us and our business partners. This digital environment is subject to breach, damage, destruction, disruption, malfunction or failure from, among other things, cyber-attacks and other unauthorized intrusions, power losses, telecommunications failures, acts of war or terror, earthquakes, fires and other natural disasters. We are continuously subjected to attempted cyber-attacks, ranging from standard phishing mails to sophisticated campaigns, such as spear phishing targeting specific Company management. While we have experienced an increase in the number of such threats and attempted cyber-attacks in recent years, which may be related to the geopolitical environment, none of these acts was believed to have had a material effect on the Company. Where required, relevant authorities were notified in accordance with the law and the relevant procedures the Company and its subsidiaries (as applicable) have in place. Our computer and communications systems, databases and users face ongoing threats of malicious software (malware), social engineering, distributed denial of service (DDoS), malicious code, zero-day vulnerabilities and other security threats and system disruptions carried out by a variety of threat actors. In particular, we have been and may continue to be targeted by nation states and experienced and skilled computer programmers and hackers, including those sponsored by or acting for foreign governments or terrorist organizations and in some cases, using artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI and agentic AI to facilitate their attacks. Such programmers and hackers attempt to penetrate or circumvent our cyber security defenses, obtain data and damage or disrupt our digital environment in order to, among other things, misappropriate or compromise our IP or other proprietary or protected information or that of our employees, customers and other business partners, prevent us from being able to use such information in our operations or demand that we pay ransom. Our suppliers are also sometimes subject to cyber-attacks, which have increased in recent years and pose a risk to those of our systems and operations that depend on such suppliers. credit_strengths.text: Gross leverage sits far below the sector median and declined year over year, reflecting a debt stock that has been steadily amortised while the EBITDA proxy expanded on higher revenue and operating income. The balance sheet carries net cash, so leverage is not a binding constraint on the credit.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure and dividends with a comfortable margin, and free cash flow covers the dividend several times over. Cash generation is the primary support for the credit, and the conversion of operating income into cash improved materially versus the prior year.

key_risks.text: Revenue is concentrated in fixed-price long-term defence design and integration contracts recognised over time under percentage-of-completion judgements, so estimate revisions on cost and control transfer can swing margins and cash. Operating margin, while improving, remains well below the sector median, leaving limited cushion against contract-level cost overruns.

The disclosed risk factors flag persistent and increasing cyber and supply-chain intrusion attempts, including nation-state and AI-enabled campaigns and a supplier incident, against a digital environment central to operations and intellectual property. A successful breach could disrupt delivery on long-term contracts and erode programme economics.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved year over year and clears unity comfortably, but remains below the sector median, reflecting a modest operating margin relative to peers. Debt service is nonetheless comfortably met, and the maturity profile is short-dated with the bulk of borrowings classified as current, so refinancing needs are modest in absolute terms.

Cash flow to debt and free cash flow to debt both improved sharply and stand far above sector medians, indicating ample capacity to retire the small debt stock from internally generated funds. Liquidity is sound, with the current ratio above both the prior year and the sector median.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal on a net cash basis, with leverage and cash-flow coverage metrics far stronger than the Industrials median. Our judgement is that the credit is anchored by recurring defence demand and cash generation rather than by balance-sheet leverage, and the trend direction is favourable.

The main sensitivities are contract-estimate and cyber-related rather than financing-driven, since dividends absorb only part of free cash flow and buyback data is unavailable, leaving distributions a secondary consideration. We view the issuer as a low-leverage, cash-generative credit whose key watch items are margin recovery toward peers and programme execution.

credit_strengths.text: 總槓桿遠低於行業中位數，並按年下降，反映債務存量已穩步攤還，而EBITDA代理則因收入及經營溢利上升而擴大。資產負債表持有淨現金，因此槓桿並非信貸的約束條件。
經營現金流以舒適的餘裕覆蓋資本開支及股息，自由現金流覆蓋股息數倍以上。現金產生是信貸的主要支撐，而經營溢利轉化為現金的能力較上一年度大幅改善。

key_risks.text: 收入集中於固定價格的長期國防設計及整合合約，按完工百分比判斷隨時間確認，因此成本及控制權轉移的估計修訂可令利潤率及現金大幅波動。經營利潤率雖有改善，但仍遠低於行業中位數，對合約層面的成本超支留下有限緩衝。
披露的風險因素指出持續且增加的網絡及供應鏈入侵企圖，包括國家級及AI驅動的攻擊活動以及一宗供應商事件，而數碼環境對營運及知識產權至關重要。一旦成功入侵，可能干擾長期合約的交付並侵蝕項目經濟效益。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年改善並舒適地高於一，但仍低於行業中位數，反映經營利潤率相對同業溫和。儘管如此，償債仍能舒適地滿足，而到期結構偏短，大部分借款分類為流動，因此再融資需求按絕對值而言溫和。
現金流對債務及自由現金流對債務均大幅改善，並遠高於行業中位數，顯示有充裕能力以內部產生的資金償還少量債務存量。流動性穩健，流動比率高於上一年度及行業中位數。

overall_credit_view.text: 按淨現金基準，指示性財務風險狀況為極低，槓桿及現金流覆蓋指標遠強於工業行業中位數。我們的判斷是，該信貸由經常性國防需求及現金產生所錨定，而非由資產負債表槓桿所支撐，而趨勢方向有利。
主要敏感因素在於合約估計及網絡相關，而非融資驅動，因為股息僅吸收部分自由現金流，且回購數據不可得，使分派成為次要考慮。我們認為該發行人為低槓桿、現金產生型信貸，其主要關注事項為利潤率向同業復甦及項目執行。
